infeasible: [Largest] The boss fog ring hides most of the plan's 'INSIDE' show. render/bossFog.ts: alpha = max(..., 0.985*(1-smoothstep(0.8,1,h))), so the wall is opaque from its foot to 80% of its height, double-sided, with a depth-only solid pass. world/gatePlan.ts:105 sets its height to min(16, max(6, 0.22*(R+1.5))), which is 6 m for R24-26, 7.4 (R32), 7.8 (R34), 10.0 (R44) and 10.9 (R48). It thickens during a fight (uHeld) and systems/bossArena.ts holdInVeil keeps the player inside it. From the fight circle a follow camera a few metres up cannot see anything lower than roughly 7-9 m at 40 m range. Hidden: Colour's revetment and terraces, Orne's lots, Martin's rail crowd and cabins, Hastur's lower tiers and audience (+1.3..7 m), Colossus's torch statues, Medusa's household statues, Bokrug's Ib-folk, Zkauba's lane detail, the mouths of Pipers' short ranks. Nearly every 'INSIDE' list item is ground-level. Fix: put the spectacle above ~12 m or on the arena floor inside R, or make ring height and alpha plan-aware (FogWall.height from the plan, a thinner solid pass where the structure is the show). Add a render capture from the fight circle as an acceptance test.

Colliders only block within their vertical range. world/colliders.ts pushOut() skips a box/obox/cylinder unless the capsule [y, y+h] overlaps [y0, y1], and falls.ts hits() does the same. Round-63 walls use y0 = pad level - 0.3 because the ground is flat for 7 m past the wall (HOUSE.level). On the plan's raised rims the ground is not flat. Colour's +6 m bank over a 14 m blend has a max slope of about 0.64 (1.5*6/14), the dune skirt (8-9 m over 24-28 m) about 0.5, and the mesa lip (14 m over 24-28 m) about 0.8. A 4.6 m chord then spans 2-4 m of ground, so a 3 m revetment (Colour) leaves a head-high gap at the low end of each chord and a step-over at the high end. padProfile must give each chord y0 = min ground over its footprint minus ~2 and y1 = max ground plus wall height. The closure test must walk with feet at ground(), not at pad level. The plan says 'a slope is no barrier' but not this.

The moat and lagoon switch on the sea-reflection pass for the whole fight. main.ts:304 sets pipeline.reflection.enabled from waterAbout(), which tests rings of 18, 55 and 110 m round the camera for ground below seaLevel-0.5 (-2.5). A -6 annulus (Black Man, 41-55 m) or lagoon (Cthulhu, 61-97 m) trips it, and the pass redraws the whole scene at half size. Today only Pipers' east edge trips it (my probe: 1 of 529 samples below -1.6). docs/PERFORMANCE.md lists reflection as a cost but autoQuality's ladder (resolution, fog, shadows) has no rung for it. Black Man is in the demo, and its heart already reads 667k triangles in docs/handoff/PERF. Needs: a measured cost, a per-plan reflection suppression or a lower reflection resolution for these two, and a ladder rung.

The triangle budget is stated in the wrong units. The 60k cap in tests/arenaHouse.test.ts counts one pass. My measurement of the current houses (setPieces over house.props) gives 14k to 45k each: Colossus 44k, Yig 45k, Cthulhu 45k, Shub 32k for 76 pieces (about 424 tris a piece). docs/handoff/PERF-arenas-main-vs-pr152.md counts every pass (moon shadow, lantern shadow, reflection) and finds 112k-667k at the hearts, 80-280 draws against the 150 ceiling, and Zkauba's heart +353k for a 34k house (noise is about +-250k). Shub's three palisades are about 1,093 m of wall against 314 m now, so about 238 pieces and about 100k tris at today's kit density, which breaks the cap. The same holds for Orne's 120 m tomb-lot grid and Zkauba's tower grid. A merged per-material mesh is never frustum-culled, and 3 sectors only partition it. There is no LOD, and the quality ladder cannot lower geometry or structure animation. Needs: a per-kit triangle target set from the multi-pass count, wall kits cut to roughly a third for mazes, a distance cull per sector, and an autoQuality rung that stops structure views and crowds.

Mazes have no foe AI to run them. There is no path planner (grep finds no pathfind or navmesh); systems/tactics.ts unstick() only sidesteps at random after AI.stuck seconds. In 5 m lanes between solid blocks any hunting foe pins itself on the first corner. Foes are posted by planSpawns (line 107 posts 3-4 at R+7..R+14 of every arena) or summoned (Orne summons reanimated_corpse). systems/mountGround.ts:16 mountPlaceForbidden is a circle of a.radius+margin, so a rig can still be ridden into the Orne, Shub and Zkauba lanes. The 4.2 m camera boom and lock-on in 5 m lanes are unchecked. The plan only BFS-checks the walls. Needs: no foes in the maze except fixed bay guards that never leave their bay, mounts forbidden by plan.inside(), a lane-width camera test, and the walk bot also run with foes present.

Circle/axis hard-wires missing from the plan's list. world/gatePlan.ts:100-106 puts the stake at R+1.5+9 = R+10.5 on the front axis, and ringCandle() puts the candle within 4.6 m of it. That conflicts with Hastur ('stake and candle on the third tier landing' while the first riser stands at R+8, inside the stake), Colossus ('first landing inside the trench mouth') and any maze whose first wall is nearer than R+14. Also circle-only: planSpawns.ts:107 (foe posts), mountGround.ts:16, mapArt.ts:152 and mapData.ts:65. The plan lists placements.ts:226, worldScene.ts:54, validateWorld.ts:107 and the tests, but not gatePlan, ringCandle, mountPlaceForbidden or planSpawns. The stake and candle should come from the plan (EnclosurePlan.stake), not from a formula.

Pad ordering and double implementation. (a) placements.ts build() pushes pads in loop order, and each region's arenas come before its dungeons. A wall's y computed at plan time (padProfile) will not include a later dungeon pad's 12 m blend or MOUND_BAND. (b) padProfile 'equal to terrain.surface' duplicates flatten() and will drift. Make flatten() call padProfile, or build every pad first and plan structures second. (c) The gate must end on land. Cthulhu's gate sits at the lagoon rim, so tests/houseWalk's courtPoint(gate, 6) and the court's first pages land on the outer bank, which is the sunk pad's blend band. The pad radius plus blend must end at the gate or those points are below -1.6 (water, drowning). The same applies to the Black Man causeway head.

Orne's grid does not 'trim' cleanly. Probe of worldLayout: curwen_catacombs' rect lies at x -140..-60, z -36..60 relative to the arena centre, so the 120 m grid (half-width 60) touches it exactly. The dungeon pad adds a 12 m blend and MOUND_BAND, and the Elder Sign prov_catacombs stands at (-103, 24) inside that area. The west third of the grid is therefore unavailable and the spanning tree has to start from a roughly 100 m by 120 m lot. The gate faces east, away from it, so this is feasible, but the plan's 'trim the grid on that side' understates it. Also check the nudge for Ancient Ones: ultimate_void's rect begins at x 112, z 24..120 (24 m off the court axis, not 'in the corridor' as the plan says), and a 14 m east nudge narrows the gap to the dungeon's mound band.

Yig's 'seven-foot sandstone doorway' leading into a 20 m tunnel through the head will not work with the follow camera. The boom is 4.2 m behind and camera margin 0.3 keeps the lens off colliders, so a 2.1 m-high, 3 m-wide, 20 m-long passage pins the lens to the player's back. The player capsule is 1.8 m. Make the mouth at least 5-6 m high, or keep the seven-foot door as a small inset inside a wide, high mouth.

Internal contradiction at Bokrug. fightGround says 'no water in the arena', but the Bokrug motion list has 'at the flood phase water rises 0.7 m'. Bokrug is one of the sea colossi whose arena floods (DECISIONS phase 5b; reality.ts flood draws a disc at ground y with radius R+2). The 8 m charge runway and 'walkable lilies' must work under the flood hook. Reword it, and decide whether the flood stops short of the parapet.

Sub-pixel motion. The internal target is 400x225 (600x338 at the default setting), and FX.snapPixels = 1 snaps vertices to a low-res pixel. At 30 m one low-res pixel is about 0.1 m. Many described motions are below that and will jitter or vanish: the hulk's 1 degree rock (0.16 m at the ends), the 0.5 m masonry course scroll, 28 mausoleum doors unlatching 20 degrees, 12-segment hair, intaglio on prisms, bark eyes, spectator faces, clock hands and calm-sway at low amplitude. Specify minimum amplitudes and use large, emissive, silhouette-level motion or particles, and verify at 400x225 with the vertex snap on.

Effort is understated against its own precedent. Round 63 was 19 houses from 9 wall kinds and 4 tower kinds, plus one gate look. The plan is about 40 outline kits, 3 maze variants with new block kits, 5 ground profiles, 3 assemblies, 19 bespoke StructureView files, 19 gate looks, 5 new shader options (new program variants and an aArc attribute that every merged geometry of that material must carry), a new place-look layer, an audio scheduler with about 9 new recipes, and about 10 new test files. Several files already exceed the 300-line rule (siteMeshes.ts is 278 and will gain sector jobs; placements.ts is 273). A realistic schedule needs a go/no-go after the three pilots (Hutchinson, Colour, Black Man) with measured costs, and parametric kits shared across places only where the places are not meant to be alike.

'External free assets' cannot supply the enclosures. The bake keeps only light/dark per face, flat shaded, with no emission or vertex colour, and only stone, wood and leaf classes (tools/models/bake_models.py). KayKit gravestones, crypt and coffin duplicate the Kenney Graveyard models already baked (crypt, crypt_small, grave_*, cross, coffin, urn, iron_fence). The real gains are dead trees, arch_gate, ribcage, and Hexagon tower, wall and gate pieces. I confirmed git ls-remote works for KayKit Halloween-Bits, Dungeon-Remastered, Medieval-Hexagon and Space-Base-Bits; kenney.nl returns 403. Tell the owner plainly that every structure is code-built and the models are dressing, and use the Hexagon castle pieces in particular if a castle is wanted.

Finding (4) is overstated. worldScene.ts:54 uses radius+12 for the site footprint, which does contradict DECISIONS round 63. But WORLD.chunk = 64 m and load = 2 chunks, and syncSites() builds the whole arena mesh once any footprint chunk is loaded. The wall at R+18 loads long before it is visible, so there is no pop-in at the current sizes. The real cost of a bigger footprint is mesh build time (one slicer job) and the un-cullable mesh. Keep the footprint change, but justify it by validateWorld and pad coverage, not streaming.

Hastur: confirmed that systems/signatures/hastur.ts:20-26 spawns him 12 m ahead of the player wherever the third band falls, and that population.ts:62 holds a called boss's arena empty only until ow.called. Until round 74 the Carcosa theatre (and the round-63 house) encloses nothing. The plan schedules this correctly. If the owner picks the alternative (keep the roaming call), drop Hastur from the 19 and give him a mobile effect instead.
lore: Hutchinson is seated in the wrong man's house. The plan builds Curwen's own Pawtuxet farm (peaked house, stack chimney, lean-to lab, slit outbuilding, oaken door in the river bank) for Edward Hutchinson, and its own note says Hutchinson lived in a Salem house 'well out toward the woods'. joseph_curwen is a separate boss in the same tile (named.ts:48; curwen_catacombs 99 m east, laboratory room), and in the novel the catacombs lie beneath that same farm. The Providence tile would show Curwen's farm twice. The plan drops Baron Ferenczy of Rakus (Transylvania) as 'unverified', having read only the first 100k characters. The game's own epitaph relies on it ('The letters from Transylvania go unanswered at last', epitaphs.ts:16), and my recollection of the novel is that Hutchinson later passes as Ferenczy of Rakus. This is not verified here, so check the text. If it holds, Rakus (a real castle, which the owner asked for) is the canon seat and the Pawtuxet farm belongs to Curwen.

Nug borrows another horror's temple. 'A squat, plain temple of black basalt blocks without a single carving' with 'a vacant onyx pedestal' is, in The Mound, the temple of Tsathoggua (the plan admits 'generalised from Tsathoggua's temple'). Tsathoggua is a boss in the game's own N'kai dungeon (dungeons.ts:227 room 'nkai', boss tsathoggua) 185-192 m away in the same region (kn_yan). That is exactly the interchangeable, borrowed structure the owner ruled out. Either give Nug and Yeb a form of their own (twins: two joined halves or two pylons with the slime troughs between; the pits of N'kai) or move the 'vacant onyx pedestal cella' to Tsathoggua's hall and keep Nug's place distinct.

Daemon Pipers: a pipe organ with a console, manuals, stops and keys is a church instrument, not Lovecraft's. The sources are the 'thin, monotonous whine of accursed flutes' and drums at Azathoth's court, and the moon-beasts' ivory flutes. The plan admits 'lore-adjacent, not lore-exact'. It also puts a second 'court of Azathoth' structure in the same Beyond tile (Azathoth 175 m away). Drop the console and keys, make it a graded colonnade of hollow ivory-and-bone flutes (reeds) played by wind and the pipers, with the gate as a passage between the largest, or accept the organ and tell the owner it is an invention.

Orne's 'Roman Wall' risk. The plan builds an old Roman-brick wall with a vault arch into a Salem burying ground because Orne's letter speaks of work 'in ye Vault, under ye Roman Wall'. A Roman wall is a European feature, not a Massachusetts one, and the letter reads as a cipher or a European locale. I could not verify this here. Check the text before building it as the enclosure, and if it is not a Salem place, keep the cemetery grid and draw the vault from the story's actual crypt.

Shub-Niggurath's labyrinth is the weakest lore link. The plan admits she is never described structurally. The actual architecture in the sources is the hilltop ring of rough-hewn columns with the table-like altar stone (Sentinel Hill), the Whateley farm and the Devil's Hop Yard (Dunwich Horror), and Dark Mountain and Lee's Swamp (Whisperer). A concentric living maze is the owner's 'mazes' request, not the story's. It also overlaps Plan C's horn-tree maze, which per the handoff wins for the Outer Gods. State that plainly, and fold the altar stone ring into the maze's heart as the plan does.

Ancient Ones: the plan's thirteen pedestals duplicate Azathoth's thirteen dancers exactly, and I cannot confirm the story gives a number (check the text of Through the Gates of the Silver Key). Plan C's design for the same horror uses a lattice of seven prisms with 'you are the missing seventh'. Pick one count (suggest seven or nine, not thirteen) and reconcile A with C. The Ultimate Gate arch also appears twice: Yog-Sothoth's bay and the existing heart trilith of the Ancient Ones' chamber. In the story the Ancient Ones sit before the Gate, so the same arch is lore-true, but the two places must not read as one set.

Bokrug conflates two cities that never stood together. In The Doom that Came to Sarnath, Sarnath's men destroyed Ib and cast its monoliths into the lake, and Ib's idol-bearing folk later destroyed Sarnath, leaving only a marsh. The plan puts Sarnath's marble wall with bronze gates fronting Ib's monolith wall, and the post-doom marsh inside. Choose one moment. The strongest is the bronze gates burst at midnight, with the marsh and the half-buried idol inside, and the monoliths as the lake side.

Smaller lore flags, none blocking. Martin's Beach: canon (a summary only) gives a bathing beach, a crowd and a holding vessel, so the pavilion, casino and festoons are the game's dressing. Medusa's Coil: Riverside in Missouri (the game's arenaSetsEarth already says Riverside), and the statue household is the game's. Yig's effigy follows Ohio's Serpent Mound, not the Oklahoma and K'n-yan of The Curse of Yig and The Mound. Hastur is Chambers and Bierce (acknowledged). Black Man: 'Orne's Gangway' as a causeway and 13 standing stones with balefires are readings, not text.

Ib/Sarnath, Colour and Black Man are the demo's two houses, so any lore change there is public first. Colour's dam, valve-tower and sluice are generic waterworks, drawn from the surveyor's reservoir, not from the Gardner farm. Keep them small and make the Gardner ruin (chimney, cellar, well, orchard) the thing the dam encloses.
alike: Azathoth, Ancient Ones, Hastur (and partly Medusa, Martin's, Bokrug): figures standing in a ring or on tiers. Azathoth has thirteen blind dancers on plinths at R+18, Ancient Ones thirteen pedestals each bearing a seated cloaked figure on a curve, Hastur about 120 masked spectators on tiers. The first two are literally the same composition (thirteen figures on plinths round a circle) and number. A third and fourth variation is the Medusa statue household, Martin's silhouette rail crowd and Bokrug's Ib-folk. Differentiate by scale and silhouette: dancers should be huge and sparse, the council small and seated within masonry, the audience a crowd on architecture.

Colour, Colossus and Yig: three 6-9 m earthen or sand ramparts round a flat floor (Colour's grey dam bank plus revetment, Colossus's dune skirt, Yig's serpent earthwork). From the fight circle all three read as a ring of earth. Yig's body sits at 14 m from the ring and its scales are the only difference. Give Colour a distinct engineered edge (a masonry dam face the whole way round, with a spillway), Colossus the columns as the dominant read, and keep Yig's head and coil as its own silhouette.

Medusa, Hutchinson, Nug, Bokrug and Yog-Sothoth: five rectangular or bay masonry enclosures of 12-16 m walls, each with a gatehouse or portal, all seen from the circle as four walls. The plan itself calls this the risk. Make at least Nug (windowless cube) and Bokrug (a curtain wall with a lake side, not four walls) non-rectangular in plan, and let Medusa be a U open on the lawn side.

Black Man and Cthulhu use the same layout: a disc of dry ground, an annular lethal water moat, a straight causeway or quay on the front axis, and the gate at the far bank (a boulder, the Door). It is also the same engine trick (nested pads, rect pad crossing, drowning). They differ in scale and dressing only. Either vary the layout (Black Man's causeway could be a ford of stepping stones, or a bridge, or a ferry-less island reached by a long descent; Cthulhu's forecourt a tilted platform) or push the moat into only one of the two.

Orne and Zkauba: the same grid-of-solid-blocks maze (seeded spanning tree from gate to an inner chamber) with different skins (low tomb lots versus tall metal towers). Both end up as lanes between boxes. Orne's blocks should be low (3 m, open sky and visible destination) so it reads as a graveyard, and Zkauba's tall and overhung with tunnels. A single algorithm should not make both feel identical to walk.

Colossus's colossal columns and Pipers' graded pipes on a plinth are both rings of tall cylinders with a lintel or open top; Medusa's portico adds a third. Differentiate with scale ratio, spacing and the top: Colossus a hypostyle with architraves, Pipers an open-topped graded horseshoe.

Effects are repeated across places. 'Lights chase round a ring' (halo chase) appears in at least eight (Colour, Martin's, Colossus, Hastur, Zkauba, Pipers, Bokrug, Ancient Ones) and 'heads/eyes turn to the player together' (instanced gaze) in five (Medusa, Martin's, Colossus, Hastur, Ancient Ones). Reserve each for one or two horrors and give the rest their own verb (collapse, drip, scrape, drain colour, reverse, swell).

Other Gods' crag ring on a mesa and Black Man's 12 m crag clusters read the same from the circle, and Shub's palisade, Orne's lots and Zkauba's towers will all be 'walls of stuff at 13-20 m'. Assign each a different dominant colour and texture; the handoff's own stills found every house a near-black slab. TEXTURE_KINDS has no marble, bark, sandstone, bone or metal, and the plan adds only 'plate'.

Unresolved Plan A/Plan C overlap. The handoff says six Outer Gods are open arenas in A and that Plan C wins for them. Plan C gives Azathoth 'the wall is the Other Gods dancing', Pipers 'the wall is an organ', Other Gods 'trilith wall and cloud lid', Ancient Ones a lattice of seven prisms, Shub a horn-tree maze. These are mostly the same enclosures as A with different mechanics, but A's numbers (thirteen pedestals, three palisades, organ console) conflict with C's.
missing: Castles. The only candidate is Hutchinson's 'fortified farm with a keep', since the Rakus castle was dropped as unverified. Carcosa became a theatre, not a citadel. If the owner meant real castles, nothing delivers one. Rakus for Hutchinson (if it is canon) or a Carcosa citadel with the theatre inside would, using the KayKit Medieval Hexagon tower, wall and gate meshes as dressing.

Underground megastructures. None is real. The plan's own finding is that nothing can be dug below about -1.0 m at 15 of 19 sites (sea -2, falls.ts drowns below -1.6), so Colossus's buried hypostyle is a dune and columns with a trench, which the plan states. It did not evaluate the existing dungeon kit as the host: roofed or 'open'-roofed rooms with doors, sconces, hall sets (round 62), sealed entrances, and the depthAudit/rayAudit/dungeonView walk audits already exist, so a true underground hall for Colossus (and Zkauba's metal city or Orne's crypts) could be a dungeon rather than a new planner plus kits. Say why it was rejected.

Portals into a boss dimension. Not delivered. Only Yog-Sothoth gets a decorative veil. The owner's rule allows a portal when the holder is itself an enclosing, lore-true structure, or when the arena lies wholly inside it. The plan rejects new regions (25 files, a Suno track), but it did not consider the cheaper existing parts: portalViews' veil shader, gateWalk, hiddenLayer, and the ultimate_void dungeon 92-199 m from the Beyond arenas (a pocket void that already exists). At least one flagship (Yog-Sothoth's arch, or Cthulhu's Door) could take the player through the veil to the arena inside a pocket pad. Offer it as a priced option rather than only a question.

Cthulhu 'out in the sea'. Delivered only as a 36 m inland lagoon 97 m from the centre, with 160-170 m of island east of it. The owner wrote 'maybe one out in the sea'. A true sea site means relocating the arena to the coast and re-running the containment audits. Priced as an option, it is the most direct answer to the owner.

Distinct materials. The plan adds one texture ('plate'). Marble, bark, red sandstone strata, bone/ivory, black glass and basalt are missing from TEXTURE_KINDS (stone, slab, wood, rot, flesh, hide, water, cloth, grass, mud, sand, snow, cobble, brick, clapboard, shingle, rock, dirt, gravel, leaves). Without them most of the 19 will be tints of stone again (the handoff stills found every house a near-black slab wall and gate). Add about 6 generated textures and a value-contrast check per place.

Nug has no external animation: 'OUTSIDE: nothing moves on the walls; a red line shows at the door sill'. This breaks the owner's rule that effects apply 'both internally and externally'. Hutchinson's and Yog's exteriors are also thin (distant flashes, a growing slit). Give every place at least two outdoor moving parts visible from the court (30-80 m).

Fairness and settings. Many new flashes (rod lightning with a global brightness flash, Cthulhu's door seam, Yog's forks, silent cloud lightning) and shakes (Azathoth's beat) are planned. The game's 'Flashes' setting (set.flashes, lightning only) and the shake setting exist, and Plan C requires settings.fxCap and nothing above 3 Hz. All new effects must be routed through them, and the Azathoth beat must not mask the noise circles. No word on this in the plan.

No structure reacts to the horror's fall (only Cthulhu's R'lyeh sinking). Owner-visible payoff is cheap here: the lights die, the veil closes, the rod goes dark, the moat drains or fills, and the structure's loop stops, through the same StructureView. Also, no Field Guide hint is planned for lethal moats, mazes or the 'bridge to nowhere' mechanics (the plan notes de/fr/es only if one is needed; it will be).

The owner's later messages in docs/handoff/HANDOFF.md: all 27 main bosses overhauled, and the Outer Gods' arenas given 'particularly unique and incomprehensible' portrayal and discovery 'like in the original lore'. Plan A keeps every discovery act 'unchanged', but six of the 19 are Outer Gods. Plan A must not freeze their acts or place their words before Plan C is reconciled.
corrections: Add a fog-aware visibility rule. World geometry and effects that matter in a fight must stand above the fog crown (6-11 m by arena radius; opaque to 80% of that) or on the arena floor, or the plan must change gatePlan's ring height and alpha per plan. Move the audience, rail crowd, torch statues, hair, doors and troughs up or inside, and attach a capture-based acceptance check from the fight circle to every place.

Add vertical ranges to the enclosure contract. Each collider chord carries y0 = min ground over its footprint minus ~2 and y1 = max ground plus wall height (from padProfile), and the closure test must walk with feet at ground(). Treat chords on slopes above ~0.4 as needing a deep foot.

Enforce a measured, multi-pass budget. Replace '60k triangles' with a per-structure main-pass cap plus a multi-pass cap taken from window.pipeline.renderer.info (the handoff's script is the model). Set a cap of about 10k tris per mile of maze wall (Shub is about 100k at today's density), a distance cull per sector, and a rung in render/autoQuality.ts that switches off structure views, crowds and the reflection pass. Report draws against the real 100-280 range, not the 150 ceiling.

Gate the reflection pass. For Black Man and Cthulhu (and any moat), suppress or lower the reflection pass inside the fight circle and the court, or measure its cost with the lagoon in view, before round 67 (it is in the demo).

Make the stake and candle outputs of the plan. Add EnclosurePlan.stake/candleSide, have gatePlan.ts:100-106 and ringCandle read them (Hastur, Colossus, mazes), and move planSpawns.ts:107, mountGround.ts:16 and mapArt.ts:152 to plan.inside()/plan.bound. Add them to the circle-hardwired list.

Pad contract: one source of truth for flatten() and padProfile (call padProfile from terrain.flatten), build all pads before planning any structure that reads them, and make every gate's courtPoint(gate, front, 6, 0) land at or above -1.0. Add a test that no planned pad overlaps a dungeon's pad blend or mound band (Orne and the Ancient Ones' nudge).

Maze rules: no spawned or summoned foe leaves a bay inside the maze; mounts refuse the footprint; lanes are 6 m or more where the camera boom and lock-on must work; the walk is capped; one lethal-free retreat route marks the way back; the walk bot and BFS run with the seal on and off. Consider cutting to two mazes (Shub and Orne), with Zkauba as an open tower field instead, so the plan's own 'a fourth would be one too many' becomes 'a third is one too many'.

Fix Hutchinson. Either seat him at Rakus (verify the novel) or in his Salem house, or keep the Pawtuxet farm and call it Curwen's, and then choose a different place for Hutchinson's own story. Do not build Curwen's farm over Curwen's catacombs.
Fix Nug and Pipers to be their own: not Tsathoggua's cella, and flutes rather than an organ console (see lore).
Fix Bokrug's flood contradiction, Yig's tunnel height (5-6 m or more), Orne's Roman wall (verify), Ancient Ones' count (reconcile with Plan C), and the Bokrug/Sarnath/Ib conflation (pick one moment).

Give causeways and quays a low kerb collider along their edges, or a camera-friendly width of at least 7 m. A 3.4 m crossing with a lethal edge and a 4 m dodge roll is an unfair death on the only way to a boss. Keep the water lethal beyond the kerb. Answer the plan's question 4 with this.

Re-order the asset round. Round 70 (CC0 bake) is listed for Orne, Hutchinson and Colour, but those are built in rounds 66, 67 and 71. Run the bake before 66, or accept re-touching 66-67. Keep it to the few models that add something (dead trees, arch_gate, ribcage, Hexagon castle pieces); do not re-bake gravestones and crypts.

Add textures, not only kits: marble (Sarnath), bark (Shub), strata sandstone (Yig, Colossus), bone/ivory (Pipers, Ancient Ones), black glass (Yog, Azathoth), plus 'plate' (Zkauba), each with a value range wide enough that two places are not both near-black.
Route all new flashes and shakes through settings.flashes, the shake setting and fxCap, keep them under 3 Hz, and tie Azathoth's beat to the noise model (never mask the 45-frame warning).
